reason: Alert 1 (java/xss) is alert-FP: The sink expression response.getWriter().println(...) + org.owasp.esapi.ESAPI.encoder().encodeForHTML(fileName) (L76-L77) applies encodeForHTML to the attacker-controlled fileName, resulting in a sanitized resolved sink value that prevents XSS execution. Alert 2 (java/path-injection) is alert-TP: The sink new File(fileName) (L73) constructs a file path from fileName (derived from user-supplied cookie via param) without sanitization or validation, meaning the resolved sink value remains attacker-controlled and susceptible to path traversal.

evidence.note: XSS sink with encodeForHTML mitigation applied to fileName derived from user input.
Path injection sink new File(fileName) using unsanitized fileName derived from user input.
